subject: kitchen sponge
title: What If You Never Replaced Your Kitchen Sponge?

scenes.text: What if you never threw out your kitchen sponge? Cleaning it wouldn't save you.
In 2017, German scientists sequenced the bacteria inside used kitchen sponges.
They found three hundred sixty-two different kinds of bacteria living in them.
In some spots, up to fifty-four billion bacteria in a single cubic centimetre, a density they compared to human feces.
And sponges their owners regularly microwaved or boiled did not have fewer bacteria. Some smelly types even increased.
The scientists' advice: replace it about once a week. That sponge on your sink is a city.

description:
What if you never replaced your kitchen sponge? A 2017 study in Scientific Reports found 362 types of bacteria in used kitchen sponges, with densities up to 54 billion cells per cubic centimetre.
Sponges that were regularly cleaned (microwaved or boiled) did not have fewer bacteria, and some odour-causing types were more common. The authors suggested replacing sponges weekly.
